key_insight: Treat cellular signaling sequences as a spatio-temporal 'video' and use generative video modeling to synthesize high‑resolution GPS trajectories from coarse cell‑tower records, recovering fine-grained routes that raw signaling lacks.
problem_solved: Converts ubiquitous but coarse cellular signaling (serving‑cell identifiers, timestamps) into accurate GPS‑level trajectories, enabling high‑precision mobility traces when direct GPS is unavailable or sparse.
method: Frame signaling sequences as a spatio‑temporal generation task and apply generative video/sequence models to predict continuous trajectory frames.
Fuse contextual priors (cell‑tower geometry, map constraints, temporal smoothness) to constrain generation and improve realism.
Train and/or fine‑tune with available GPS ground truth (supervised or self‑supervised alignment) and evaluate against standard trajectory baselines.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to unlock large-scale mobility insights from low‑cost signaling data without pervasive GPS, improving applications in urban planning, transportation analytics, and location‑based services while raising new considerations for privacy and responsible use.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: raw cellular signals → video-generation model → reconstructed GPS trajectory
Map overlay: coarse cell‑tower coverage (polygons) vs. reconstructed high‑resolution route
Error comparison chart: reconstruction error (e.g., mean distance) vs. baseline methods
Temporal visualization: animation or frame sequence showing progressive refinement of trajectory predictions
paper_title: Think over Trajectories: Leveraging Video Generation to Reconstruct GPS Trajectories from Cellular Signaling
paper_authors: Ruixing Zhang, Hanzhang Jiang, Leilei Sun, Liangzhe Han, Jibin Wang
